method: Automated inventory read every source, evidence, pathway, profile and review record in the exact manifest candidate for this ISO.

source_refs.locator: Printed pp. 24–25, returnee impacts perceived by Goluj residents

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2002 reports: After the border war disrupted transhumance and Tekezze-Setit basin watering access, herds shifted to wells around Goluj and nearby return sites; the study reports emerging farmer–livestock-owner conflict.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2002 reports: Rapid borehole development in Gash-Barka changed water use and encouraged larger livestock populations; the study cautioned that resource pressure could threaten poor returnee and stayee livelihoods.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: Printed pp. 20–21, fuelwood availability, access and household response

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2002 reports: Around Goluj, respondents linked scarcer fuelwood to population-related forest depletion; poor households lacking transport or money reduced use, while animal owners could access markets.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 2–3 (one-based), Anseba climate and livelihood context

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2012-11 reports: UNDP’s case study reports erratic below-average rain in 2002–2004, especially in parts of Habero, caused livestock losses and impaired livelihoods; annual rain ranged from 190 mm in Habero to about 367 mm in Hamelmalo.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 2 (one-based), Anseba pastoral movements and land-use context

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2012-11 reports: Anseba herders moved west in July–September and toward the eastern escarpment or Northern Red Sea in November–March; land-use pressure, degradation and settlement policies disrupted this practice.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2024-03 reports: For solar-asset planning, GCA describes lowland and coastal rainfall below 100 mm with dry spells over 200 days, versus wetter highlands; drought hazard is very high across most Eritrea and dust/wind risk is elevated in Anseba.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2024-03 reports: For 2030–2060, mean annual rainfall is projected to fall by up to 100 mm on the Eritrean Plateau, with slight increases in western lowlands and southern areas; wet-day changes are small under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

pathways.compact_statement: Near Goluj, border-war restrictions narrowed seasonal livestock water access and concentrated local resource pressures; findings are historical and exceptional.
alternative_explanations: Borehole siting, herd numbers, settlement patterns and crop-residue management also shaped pressure.
pathways.uncertainty: Historical dryland coping mechanism from 1999–2001 research, not measured climate-change impact, current violence or an evaluated adaptation project.
recommendations: Keep the reverse mechanism bounded to the named institution, population and place supported by its cited evidence; do not infer violence from climate vulnerability.
Retain only evidence whose documented geography supports the pathway location; otherwise narrow the pathway or keep the evidence standalone.
